Conflicted

/kuhn-FLIK-tid/ - the stress falls on FLIK · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Conflicted means torn between opposing feelings or loyalties.

Otis felt conflicted at the auction: bidding on the vintage press meant outbidding the museum where he had volunteered for years.

Worked Example

Offered the anchor chair in another city, the reporter was openly conflicted — the job she had chased for a decade on one side, her mother's Sunday dinners and her hometown sources on the other.

Conflicted is stronger and more specific than 'unsure': it means two loyalties or desires are at war inside you, so that serving either one feels like betraying the other.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

divided: Divided means split between sides — a committee, a family, or a single mind pulled toward opposing camps. Conflicted is more personal and more painful: the split runs between loyalties, so that serving either one feels like betraying the other. A vote can be divided; a heart is conflicted.

split: Split means cut cleanly into two camps or impulses — the sharpest, plainest version of being of two minds. Conflicted adds the ache: its two sides are loyalties or duties at war, so the person suffers the split rather than simply containing it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

single-minded: driven by exactly one aim

untroubled: free of any inner struggle at all

Where it sits · how painful the inner struggle grows — uneasy → conflicted → anguished

uneasy vs. conflicted: Uneasy is fainter than conflicted — a low hum of discomfort without two loyalties actually at war.

anguished vs. conflicted: Anguished goes further than conflicted: the inner tug-of-war has broken into open pain.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: together

Root — flict-

Root — flict-: to strike (Latin fligere)

Suffix — -ed

Suffix — -ed: made to be

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (together) + flict- (to strike) + -ed = struck together. Two loyalties collide inside one person like flint on steel — the whole conflict happens within.

Use the root in a new word: inflict

Use the root in a new word: inflict: The hailstorm inflicted more damage in ten minutes than the whole rainy season had.

Word Choice

neutral

Conflicted is the word for loyalty pulled two ways — job against family, evidence against sympathy. Where its unit-mate ambivalent reports mixed feelings, conflicted stages a fight between them; the stakes are duties, not just moods.
